**Yoga Coach Feedback:**

*"Great effort in Warrior One, [Student’s Name]! You’re really building strength and focus in this pose—let’s refine a few things to help you find even more stability and alignment. Here’s what we’ll work on together:*

1. **Spine Alignment:** *I notice your spine is slightly rounded or leaning forward. To improve this, gently draw your tailbone down toward the mat while lifting your chest and crown of the head upward. Imagine a string pulling you tall from the top of your head—this will help lengthen your spine and keep it neutral. Engage your core lightly to support this alignment.*

2. **Arm Position:** *Your arms are close, but let’s straighten them fully overhead. Reach up through your fingertips as if you’re trying to touch the ceiling, keeping your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears. If your shoulders feel tight, you can slightly widen your hands—just ensure your arms are straight and active.*

3. **Knee Over Ankle:** *Your front knee is drifting slightly forward past your ankle. To correct this, press firmly through your back foot and shift your weight back just enough so your knee stacks directly over your ankle. This protects your knee joint and builds strength in the legs. If needed, shorten your stance a little to find that alignment.*

*Take a deep breath in, and as you exhale, make these adjustments one at a time. You’ve got this! Warrior One is all about strength and grace—let’s embody both. How does that feel in your body?"*

*(Pause for their response, then offer encouragement like:)*
*"Perfect! You’re already looking more grounded and powerful. Keep breathing deeply—this pose is yours to own."*
